Q731.L1t: The passage is about product safety problems in goods made in China and the reactions to them.
Q731.L2t: The passage says melamine was found in wheat flour used to make pet food sold in North America.
Q731.L3t: The passage names toxic medicine in Panama, toothpaste with the antifreeze chemical, melamine in pet food, restricted seafood imports and toys with lead paint, and a careful reader counts these distinct cases.
Q731.L4t: The passage mentions five cases of safety problems.
Q731.L2f: The passage says the pet food problem was caused by lead paint on the packaging and affected only cats in Europe.
Q731.L3f: The passage lists six separate safety cases because it counts the corruption case of the former drug agency head as a product safety problem of its own.
Q731.L4f: The passage mentions six cases of safety problems.

Q835.L1t: The letter is written by a visitor from Mars who describes the strange habits of life on Earth in a humorous way.
Q835.L2t: In the letter the Martian says that people leave their big boxes every morning and get into smaller boxes on wheels.
Q835.L3t: The Martian sees the small boxes race around and then stop to rest, and since he describes everything in terms of boxes, he is describing things with wheels that people ride in and park, which he sees as boxes with wheels in them.
Q835.L4t: The small boxes on wheels are the Martian's way of describing boxes that have wheels in them.
Q835.L2f: The letter says the Martian was angry about the football game and wrote to complain to the people who run the planet.
Q835.L3f: The Martian says the small boxes on wheels are body parts that people use to hear sounds while they race around and rest.
Q835.L4f: The small boxes on wheels are ears.

Q765.L1t: The passage is about apologies, forgiveness and healing between people, based on a talk by a spiritual researcher.
Q765.L2t: Caroline Myss says that saying "I never meant to hurt you" is not a sufficient apology, even though it may keep a friendship going.
Q765.L3t: After criticizing the weak apology, Myss redoes the scene and shows a soul-to-soul confession that admits knowing what you did and asks for forgiveness, which is a guide to the way to apologize that really heals.
Q765.L4t: The author's purpose is to tell people how to apologize sincerely.
Q765.L2f: Caroline Myss says that the phrase "I never meant to hurt you" is the best way to apologize and that it heals the other person's soul.
Q765.L3f: The passage spends almost all of its length listing the reasons why people are unable to say "I never meant to hurt you", and it offers no alternative way of speaking to the person who was hurt.
Q765.L4f: The author's purpose is to explain why people can't say "I never meant to hurt you".
